Method of Attack: Phishing kit that simulates file archiver software (e.g. WinRAR) in the browser using .zip domains to trick users into opening malicious files
Displays fake in-browser WinRar and Windows File Explorer windows to convince users they opened a ZIP archive
Uses fake security scan button to appear legitimate
Redirects users to credential theft pages or delivers malware by disguising .exe files as PDFs
Exploits Windows behavior of opening searched-for strings as URLs if no local file is found
Attack Vector: Phishing via fake ZIP domain websites
Malware delivery through disguised executable downloads
Credential theft via fake file viewer interfaces
Indicators of Compromise: Use of .zip TLD domains such as bleepingcomputer.zip
Fake WinRar or Windows File Explorer windows displayed in browser
Links like setup.zip redirecting to malicious sites
Downloaded files named like document.pdf.exe disguised as PDFs
